title: MedicaLogic Viral Health Myth Record (v2)
description: One record = one viral health claim, its manipulation markers, and the PubMed evidence used to check it. Verdicts are literature-based syntheses of several sources, not medical rulings. Scope: health MISinformation (false or inaccurate, whatever the intent) that could lead to harm.

claim_text.description: The claim in one neutral sentence (what the post says is true).

category.description: Topic bucket, e.g. detox, vaccines, nutrition, infection, cancer, mental-health

platform_origin.description: Every platform where the claim was seen.

source_url.description: Optional link to an example post.

date_observed.description: When the claim was seen trending (YYYY-MM-DD).

raw_quotes.description: Exact wording copied from the post/video.

manipulation_markers.description: Phrases FROM THE POST (not from the article). Feeds the Emotional Manipulation Meter.

mechanism.description: What the science actually says about how this works.

risk_classification.description: How much harm could someone come to by believing this?

risk_rationale.description: One sentence explaining the risk level.

verdict.description: Synthesis of all sources. Divergent = evidence is mixed. Insufficient = not enough verified evidence (a valid result).

relevance.description: Does the study test this claim directly, or support it from another angle (mechanism, safety)?

note.description: One line: what this study shows about the claim.

recommended_action.description: Safe, practical advice for the reader (no diagnosis).

advice_source.description: Link to the trusted source of the recommended action.

true_part.description: What is actually true or based on real science (Jiayi: many myths start from real science).

overstated_part.description: What the claim stretches beyond the evidence.

safety_pmids.description: Extra PMIDs cited for the risk section.

evidence_last_checked.description: Date the evidence was last checked on PubMed.

pmid_verified.description: True once every PMID was opened on PubMed and its title matched (run verify_pmids.py).

needs_review.description: Fields drafted or unclear that a researcher still needs to confirm.

information_disorder_type.description: Challenge definitions: misinformation = false or inaccurate whatever the intent; disinformation = spread on purpose to harm; malinformation = true information taken out of context to harm.

core.description: One of the 5 core benchmark claims (multi-source, team-verified).
